name: Undersea cables & GPS
value: SMW5 cable fault off Pakistan since 18 Nov
summary: A submarine cable fault 11km off Pakistan has slowed internet since 18 Nov; no cause given, no sabotage confirmed
state: Pakistan's telecoms authority said on 19 Nov that a fault on an international submarine cable about 11km from the shore was causing intermittent connectivity problems, giving no restoration time (Radio Pakistan). The National linked the fault to the SMW5 system and reported Cloudflare Radar data showing traffic falls of up to 36% from 18 Nov. Searches on 28 Nov found no restoration announcement for this fault, no multiple cuts isolating a region and no confirmed sabotage.
for_you: Users and businesses in Pakistan may see slower international connections while traffic is rerouted. Cable faults are usually repaired within weeks once a repair ship reaches the site.
rubric_hit: Cable damage incident (SMW5 fault off Pakistan from 18 Nov): Watch; no multiple cuts or confirmed sabotage

sources.title: Radio Pakistan — Submarine cable fault may affect internet services in Pakistan: PTA
The National — Pakistan internet problems linked to subsea cable fault

why: Subsea cables carry ~99% of intercontinental data; GPS jamming affects aviation and shipping.
drivers: Anchor drags, sabotage, conflict-zone jamming and spoofing.

rubric.alert: Multiple cable cuts isolating a region, or confirmed sabotage.
rubric.watch: Cable damage incident, or widespread GNSS interference affecting aviation.
rubric.normal: No new cable cuts or major jamming escalations.
